title: Micah, the House of God, and the Levitical Priest
description: A man named Micah from the hill country of Ephraim confesses to his mother that he took eleven hundred silver pieces from her. When he returns the silver, his mother dedicates it to the Lord, and two hundred silver pieces are used so a silversmith makes a carved image and a cast idol, which is placed in Micah's house. Micah sets up a shrine with an ephod and household gods, and first appoints one of his sons as priest. The narrator notes that in those days there was no king in Israel; everyone did what was right in their own eyes. Later, a young Levite from Bethlehem in Judah passes by looking for a place to stay, and Micah hires him as priest for ten silver pieces a year, along with clothing and food. Micah now believes the Lord will do good to him because he has a Levite serving as his priest.
